<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title. Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore. -->

## Motivation

With speculative decoding, `compute_spec_logprobs` returns the top logprobs as one GPU tensor slice per row, and there are `bs x num_draft_tokens` rows per step. Each step then pays one pinned allocation and one D2H copy per row in `GenerationBatchResult.copy_to_cpu`, and one `.tolist()` per row in the decode result path. For clients that ask for top-k logprobs on every token, this host-side work grows with batch size and draft length and slows the scheduler.

## Modifications

- `compute_spec_logprobs`: when every request in the batch asks for the same `top_logprobs_num = k`, keep the result as one `[rows, k]` value / index tensor pair from a single `topk(k)`. This is the same call `get_top_logprobs` makes (with `max_k == k`, its per-row `[:k]` slices are whole rows), so the values, ids and tie order are unchanged. Batches with mixed `k` keep the per-row path.
- `GenerationBatchResult.copy_to_cpu`: a `[rows, k]` tensor moves with one copy; a per-row list as before.
- `SchedulerBatchResultProcessor`: one helper converts either form to host lists of rows (one `.tolist()` for the tensor). The consumers keep indexing `top_logprobs_val[row]`.
- `LogitsProcessorOutput.next_token_top_logprobs_{val,idx}`: type comment updated.
- New CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/layers/test_logprob_processor_spec_top_logprobs.py`: the batched rows equal the per-row path bit for bit (greedy and temperature, ties, chain and `accept_index` layouts, k = 1, 5, 8, 32), and mixed-k batches keep row lists.

## Accuracy Tests

Identical outputs vs upstream main `8d4e1ce4c7` for a fixed batch composition, same GPU and container, `--enable-deterministic-inference`. The batched path makes the same `topk` call, so values, ids and tie order are unchanged for the same rows; across different batch compositions (concurrent requests landing in different batches) tied top-k entries (equal logprob) may come out in a different order, on main as on this PR. 1x GB300, `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` + EAGLE3 draft `Tengyunw/qwen3_30b_moe_eagle3`. Four concurrent batches of 6 prompts x 64 tokens: `top_logprobs_num` 5, 20, mixed 5/20/none, and 20 with temperature 0.7 + `sampling_seed`. Output ids, output token logprobs and top logprobs (values and ids) compared as JSON bytes.

| EAGLE3 layout | result |
|---|---|
| chain (`--speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`) | identical, 24/24 requests (byte-identical dumps in our runs) |
| tree (`--speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 4 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 8`) | identical, 24/24 requests (byte-identical dumps in our runs) |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

1x GB300, same model and chain EAGLE3 config, default server flags. Arms in order main, PR, PR, main; 2 runs per launch.

```
python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random-ids \
  --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
  --num-prompts 320 --max-concurrency 64 --seed {1,2} --return-logprob --top-logprobs-num 20
```

| | output tok/s (median of 4) | median TPOT (ms) | median TTFT (ms) | accept length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main `8d4e1ce4c7` | 1627.4 (1584.1-1648.7) | 31.26 | 583 | 1.35 |
| this PR | 2034.2 (2024.0-2053.0) | 27.03 | 318 | 1.35 |
| change | **+25.0 %** | -13.5 % | -45 % | same |

Same command and arms on 1x H100 80GB (x86 host):

| | output tok/s (median of 4) | median TPOT (ms) | accept length |
|---|---|---|---|
| main `8d4e1ce4c7` | 1517.5 (1515.3-1537.3) | 33.0 | 1.35 |
| this PR | 1497.8 (1489.4-1520.2) | 34.2 | 1.35 |
| change | -1.3 % (run spread overlaps) | | same |

The gain is on the GB300 host (Grace CPU), where the per-row host work bounded the scheduler; on the H100 node the host was not the bottleneck and there is no measurable change.
Requests without logprobs, or batches whose requests ask different `k`, run the same code as before.

Not tested: pipeline parallelism. With PP the field now crosses stages as one tensor in the PP proxy dict instead of a list of tensors; no PP run was made.

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No user-visible change.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+"""Speculative top logprobs with one k for the whole batch come back as one
+[rows, k] tensor pair. After the host copy and list conversion, every row must
+equal the per-row path (mixed k) bit for bit: values, ids and tie order.
+"""
+
+import struct
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.logprob_processor import compute_spec_logprobs
+from sglang.srt.managers.scheduler_components.batch_result_processor import (
+    _top_logprobs_to_lists,
+)
+from sglang.srt.managers.utils import _rows_d2h
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=10, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+VOCAB = 64
+
+
+def _bits(row):
+    return struct.pack(f"<{len(row)}d", *row)
+
+
+def _batch(nums, greedy):
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        seq_lens=[8] * len(nums),
+        top_logprobs_nums=list(nums),
+        token_ids_logprobs=None,
+        sampling_info=SimpleNamespace(
+            is_all_greedy=greedy,
+            temperatures=torch.tensor([0.6 + 0.1 * i for i in range(len(nums))]).view(
+                -1, 1
+            ),
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+def _host_rows(nums, greedy, logits, predict, **layout):
+    out = SimpleNamespace(
+        next_token_logits=logits.clone(),
+        next_token_top_logprobs_val=None,
+        next_token_top_logprobs_idx=None,
+    )
+    compute_spec_logprobs(_batch(nums, greedy), out, predict.clone(), **layout)
+    batched = torch.is_tensor(out.next_token_top_logprobs_val)
+    out.next_token_top_logprobs_val = _rows_d2h(out.next_token_top_logprobs_val)
+    out.next_token_top_logprobs_idx = _rows_d2h(out.next_token_top_logprobs_idx)
+    _top_logprobs_to_lists(out)
+    return batched, out.next_token_top_logprobs_val, out.next_token_top_logprobs_idx
+
+
+class TestSpecTopLogprobsBatched(CustomTestCase):
+    def _case(self, *, k, greedy, ties, chain, bs=5, max_accept=4, seed=0):
+        """Run bs requests with one k (batched path), and the same bs requests
+        plus one extra request asking k=0 (per-row path): every accepted row of
+        the first bs requests must be identical."""
+        g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+        rows = (bs + 1) * max_accept
+        logits = torch.randn(rows, VOCAB, generator=g)
+        if ties:
+            logits = (logits * 2).round() / 2
+        predict = torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (rows,), generator=g)
+
+        # Rows padded with -1 in accept_index are never read by the consumers.
+        accepted = [
+            i * max_accept + j
+            for i in range(bs)
+            for j in range(max_accept if chain else 1 + i % max_accept)
+        ]
+
+        def layout(n):
+            if chain:
+                return dict(chain_stride=max_accept)
+            accept_index = torch.full((n, max_accept), -1, dtype=torch.int32)
+            for i in range(n):
+                accept_len = 1 + i % max_accept
+                accept_index[i, :accept_len] = torch.arange(
+                    i * max_accept, i * max_accept + accept_len
+                )
+            return dict(accept_index=accept_index)
+
+        n_rows = bs * max_accept
+        batched, val, idx = _host_rows(
+            [k] * bs, greedy, logits[:n_rows], predict[:n_rows], **layout(bs)
+        )
+        per_row, ref_val, ref_idx = _host_rows(
+            [k] * bs + [0], greedy, logits, predict, **layout(bs + 1)
+        )
+        self.assertTrue(batched)
+        self.assertFalse(per_row)
+        self.assertEqual(len(val), n_rows)
+        for r in accepted:
+            self.assertEqual(idx[r], ref_idx[r])
+            self.assertEqual(_bits(val[r]), _bits(ref_val[r]))
+        self.assertTrue(all(type(t) is int for row in idx for t in row))
+
+    def test_temperature(self):
+        self._case(k=5, greedy=False, ties=False, chain=False)
+
+    def test_greedy_ties(self):
+        self._case(k=8, greedy=True, ties=True, chain=False)
+
+    def test_chain_layout(self):
+        self._case(k=8, greedy=False, ties=True, chain=True)
+
+    def test_top1_and_wide_k(self):
+        self._case(k=1, greedy=False, ties=True, chain=False, seed=1)
+        self._case(k=32, greedy=False, ties=True, chain=True, bs=7, seed=2)
+
+    def test_mixed_k_keeps_row_lists(self):
+        logits = torch.randn(4, VOCAB)
+        out = SimpleNamespace(
+            next_token_logits=logits,
+            next_token_top_logprobs_val=None,
+            next_token_top_logprobs_idx=None,
+        )
+        compute_spec_logprobs(
+            _batch([3, 0], greedy=False),
+            out,
+            torch.tensor([1, 2, 3, 4]),
+            chain_stride=2,
+        )
+        self.assertIsInstance(out.next_token_top_logprobs_val, list)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [len(v) for v in out.next_token_top_logprobs_val], [3, 3, 0, 0]
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
